newsitem.title: USA: Jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans filing first-time claims for state unemployment benefits rose by 11,000 last week, the Labour Department said Thursday, posting an unexpectedly large jump from the previous week.
Jobless claims rose to 340,000 in the week ended Sept. 21, up from 329,000 the week before, the department said. Wall Street economists had expected claims to edge down to 328,000.

The closely followed four-week moving average of claims -- considered a more accurate yardstick because it smooths out weekly fluctuations -- rose 2,500 to 328,750, from a revised 326,250 the previous week.
The Labour Department said eight states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Sept. 14, the latest period for which the data are available.
Among the largest were North Carolina, with an increase of 10,671 initial jobless claims, California, with 7,962, South Carolina, with 3,315, New York, with 3,168, and New Jersey, with 1,893.
North Carolina linked its big jump in claims to layoffs in the construction, textile and apparel industries. Claims were also reported to be related to Hurricane Fran, the department said.
California attributed its large increase to the return to a five-day workweek after a shorter reporting period in the previous Labour Day holiday week, as well as to layoffs in agriculture.
South Carolina reported layoffs in the textile industry, while New Jersey said it had layoffs in the trade and service industries. New York had no comment.

Labour said two states and one territory reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the September 14 week. They were Puerto Rico, with 1,649 fewer jobless claims, Ohio, with 1,516, and Wisconsin, with 1,230.

Puerto Rico said claims activity dropped due to Hurricane Hortense. Ohio had no comment, while Wisconsin said it had fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries, and in manufacturing.
